framework: Professor Adow TVET — Shapes and Measurements
note: A CROSS-TRADE core module, not a carpentry one. Measuring, setting out, area, volume and estimating are the same skills in a joinery shop, a welding bay, an irrigation trench and a dairy processing room — only the units and the tolerances change, so every worked example below names the trade it comes from. This is the numeracy every department's practical work rests on, and it is taught once.
source: Written for Professor Adow TVET, 2026-09-23. Structure modelled on the Ehel Academy Mathematics Stage 4 Shape and Measures lesson (geometry and measurement taught through drawn, manipulable figures rather than worked symbols), with every context replaced by a trade one.
Unit codes in leadsToFramework are from the Republic of Kenya Competency Based Curriculum for Carpentry and Joinery Level 4, ISCED 0732 354 (TVET CDACC). Cited, never reproduced.
terminology: UK / East African. Millimetres and metres, square metres, cubic metres and litres. Tape, rule, try square, spirit level, plumb bob.

assessmentModes.knowledge: The platform can assess this in full.
assessmentModes.both: The platform assesses the knowledge half; an assessor signs off the performance at the bench or on site.
assessmentModes.practical: The platform teaches and rehearses it; competence is assessed ONLY with real tools on real work. The app must never report this as certified.

weightingNote: This module is deliberately MORE app-assessable than a trade module, and that is a fact about measurement rather than a softening of the 30:70 rule. Reading a scale, converting a unit and calculating a quantity are done correctly or not, and a screen can tell which. Holding a tape true over four metres, or reading a level on a real wall, cannot be — those stay practical. The split below reflects that honestly rather than flattering it.

leadsToFramework.title: Carpentry and Joinery Level 4 (Kenya, TVET CDACC)
leadsToFramework.note: The only published framework sourced for this school so far. The other five departments' frameworks are not in hand, so a criterion that plainly serves them carries no leadsTo rather than a guessed one — an empty field here means 'not yet mapped', never 'not relevant'.

modules.title: Shapes and Measurements
modules.description: Reading a measurement, converting between units, working out area and volume, proving a corner square and a surface level, and estimating the materials a job needs. Solids, their flat developments, and the angles a job turns through.

criteria.text: Read a steel rule or tape to the nearest millimetre, naming the value rather than the nearest mark.
Take a measurement from a true end or datum, never from a damaged end or the tape's own hook when it is bent.
State the tolerance a job allows and say whether a given measurement is inside it.
criteria.evidence: Written test against a stated tolerance.

criteria.text: Hold a tape true over a long span, without sag or twist, and repeat the measurement to check it.
Convert between millimetres, centimetres and metres without changing the quantity.
Work in ONE unit throughout a calculation and state which unit an answer is in.
Convert between square metres and square millimetres, and between cubic metres and litres, correctly.
Recognise an answer whose unit is impossible for the quantity asked, and say why.
Calculate the perimeter of a rectangle and of an L-shaped room, and say what a perimeter is used for.
Calculate the area of a rectangle, a triangle and a circle, in the unit the job uses.
Find the area of an irregular shape by splitting it into rectangles, and check the split accounts for the whole.
criteria.evidence: Worked calculation with the split shown.

criteria.text: Subtract openings — a door, a window, a hatch — from a surface area before ordering material.
criteria.evidence: Take-off sheet checked against a drawing.

criteria.text: Calculate the volume of a rectangular solid and of a cylinder.
Convert a volume in cubic metres to litres, and say where each unit is the one actually used.
Work out the mass of a quantity of material from its volume and its density.
Measure a vessel or an excavation and calculate its capacity from the measurements taken.
criteria.evidence: Measurements taken on site, calculation checked.

criteria.text: Name a right angle, and explain what square, level and plumb each mean and which tool proves each.
Read a spirit level, including which way the work must move to bring the bubble central.
Prove a rectangle square by measuring both diagonals, and say what an unequal pair means.
Check a level or a square against a known reference before trusting it, and reverse it to find its own error.
Set out a right angle on the ground using the 3-4-5 rule, and say why any multiple of 3, 4 and 5 works.
criteria.evidence: Set out and checked on site.

criteria.text: Calculate the number of units — boards, blocks, tiles, plants, containers — a measured area or length requires.
Add an allowance for waste and cutting to an estimate, and state the percentage used.
Present an estimate that shows the measurements, the working and the answer, so another person can check it.
criteria.evidence: Take-off sheet checked by an assessor.

criteria.text: Name the faces, edges and vertices of a solid, and count each for a given solid.
Recognise the net of a solid and say which solid it folds into — and which nets do not fold into anything.
Mark out the development of a simple open tray or duct to stated internal sizes, allowing for the thickness of the material.
criteria.evidence: Marked-out development on sheet or card, measured against the stated sizes.

criteria.text: Explain why a development is marked and cut flat before any bend is made, and what a bend in the wrong place costs.

units.title: Angles other than the right angle

criteria.text: Name an angle as acute, right, obtuse or reflex, and prove a right angle rather than judging it by eye.
Measure an angle to the nearest degree with a protractor or angle finder, reading the correct scale of the two.
Set a sliding bevel to an existing angle and transfer it to the work without reading a number.
criteria.evidence: Observed at the bench; transferred angle checked.

criteria.text: Work out the angle each half of a mitre is cut at, from the angle the corner has to turn through.
